actual_use_paragraphs: [F2] The string decomposition of $v$ is $v=v$ with $v\in\ker E_1$, and that of $w$ is $w=F_1^{(1)}v$; hence $\tilde e_1v=0$, $\tilde f_1v=w$, $\tilde e_1w=v$, $\tilde f_1w=0$, and $\mathcal L(\omega)=A_0v\oplus A_0w$ is a crystal lattice with crystal basis the classes of $v$ and $w$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]], [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]).

[F5] For a label module with $E_1=F_1=0$ the Kashiwara operators vanish and every $A_0$-submodule is operator stable; $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ is a DVR with units the fractions with nonzero value at $0$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

[F2] On $M$ the operators are given by the unique admissible string decomposition, $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$, with $p_{\mathrm{top}},p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ preserving the lattice $L$; the operators shift weights by $\mp\alpha_i$, and every element of $M$ lies in a finite sum of string positions ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]).

Let $A_0$ be the local ring of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]] and let $M$ be an integrable weight module with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]).

[F1] $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphisms of $M$ shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$ and $-\alpha_i$; on a string they move $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ or $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$, with the top of an $\tilde e_i$-string and the bottom of an $\tilde f_i$-string mapped to $0$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]).

For the canonical objects, $B(\lambda)=\mathcal B(\lambda)$ denotes the crystal of the simple highest weight module $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]) and $P^+$ the dominant integral labels ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); that $B(\lambda)$ is a highest weight crystal of highest weight $\lambda$ is the next theorem. The operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ used throughout are those of [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]. No choice principle is used.

[F1] $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ and on $U_q^-$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the lattice $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, respectively $\mathcal L(\infty)$, once (b) is known, and lowers the weight, respectively the root degree, by $\alpha_i$; on $U_q^-$ it is injective with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]).

Let $B_1$ and $B_2$ be crystals, meaning the data $(B,wt,\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i,\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i)$ attached to a crystal basis $(L,B)$ of an integrable module by [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]] and [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $wt:B\to P$ is the weight function, $\varepsilon_i(b)=\max\{n:\tilde e_i^nb\ne0\}$ and $\varphi_i(b)=\max\{n:\tilde f_i^nb\ne0\}$ are finite, $\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle$, and $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ are the partial maps $B\to B\cup\{0\}$ of [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]].

[F4] Kashiwara operators are defined through the string decomposition; on a $2$-step string with first step coefficient $1$ and second step coefficient $[2]$, the operator $\tilde f_i$ moves one position with coefficient $1$ and $\tilde e_i$ is its inverse on the string; at the endpoints it acts by $0$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]], [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]], part (iii)).

[F1] The standard crystal ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]): $V(\lambda_1)$ is the three-dimensional integrable simple with highest weight vector of weight $\lambda_1$, and its crystal is $B(\lambda_1)=\{u_1,u_2,u_3\}$ with weights $\lambda_1,\lambda_2-\lambda_1,-\lambda_2$ and arrows $u_1\xrightarrow{1}u_2\xrightarrow{2}u_3$.
**Given:** The datum of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, the module $V=L_1(2)$ with basis $v_2,v_1,v_0$ and the operators of [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]].

[F2] A vector $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible string decomposition $u=\sum_nF_1^{(n)}u_n$ with $u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_1}=\ker E_1\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_1}$; the operators act by $\tilde e_1(\sum_nF_1^{(n)}u_n)=\sum_{n\ge1}F_1^{(n-1)}u_n$ and $\tilde f_1(\sum_nF_1^{(n)}u_n)=\sum_{n\ge0}F_1^{(n+1)}u_n$ ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]], [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]).

[F2] $V(m\omega)=L_1(m)$ has divided basis $v_t=F_1^{(t)}v_m$ with $\tilde e_1v_t=v_{t-1}$, $\tilde f_1v_t=v_{t+1}$ for the string positions and endpoint zeros, and $\mathcal L(m\omega)=A_0v_0\oplus\cdots\oplus A_0v_m$ with residue basis $\mathcal B(m\omega)$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]], part (iii), [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]).

**Given:** The rank-one Fock model $I^+=\{0,1\}$, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$, its four monomials, the residue functors $f_0,e_0$ of [[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]], the crystal of [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]] and [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]], and the head/socle behavior of [[lem-the-local-affine-hecke-socle-argument-for-residue-translations]].

[F5] The canonical crystals over the highest weight lattice ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]): $B(2)$ is the three-element one-colour chain of weights $2\lambda_1,0,-2\lambda_1$, and $B(0)$ the one-element crystal of weight $0$ fixed by both operators.

[F2] The projection $\pi_\lambda$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear with $\pi_\lambda(\mathbf 1)=v_\lambda$, and on the negative half $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the operators are the string operators with $\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i$ and $\ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]).

[F4] Crystal lattice and basis axioms ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) and the Kashiwara operators ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]) supplying the underlying finite strings and partial inverses of the two factors.

- The suppliers [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]], [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]
  and [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]] are batch-5/6 items still under
  construction at authoring time; the exact uses are the tensor rule of step 3.1
  and the lattice formalism of step 3.1, and the decision stays escalated until
  they are completed and rechecked.

[F2] Kashiwara operators ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]): on the unique admissible decomposition $v=\sum_nF_i^{(n)}v_n$ one has $\tilde e_iv=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}v_n$ and $\tilde f_iv=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}v_n$ (divided powers), both linear and shifting label weight by $\alpha_i$ and $-\alpha_i$; they preserve $L$ by [F1] and commute with module homomorphisms.

[F2] Crystal basis axioms ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]): $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ are partial maps $B\to B\cup\{0\}$ with $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$; the underlying module strings are finite and the Kashiwara operators of [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]] act as string shifts.

[F6] Crystal graph conventions ([[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]) and the Kashiwara operators ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]): $\tilde e_i$ shifts weight by $+\alpha_i$ on vertices, $\varepsilon_i(b)=\max\{n:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\ne0\}$, and the operators act as shifts on the finite module strings.

[F4] Kashiwara operators ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]): on the unique admissible string decomposition, $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ shift the divided string positions down and up by one; they are linear, preserve $L$ and commute with module homomorphisms.

[F3] Module operators: $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}}$, $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$, $\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i$, $\ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i$, and the string of an $E_i$-highest vector of rank-one weight $a$ has the positions $0,\dots,a$; the negative-half operators satisfy $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$, $\tilde e_iu=0$ iff $u\in\ker e_i'$, and $\tilde e_i$ lowers the root height by one ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]).

[F4] Crystal labels ([[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]], [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]], [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]], [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]]): the Fock Chevalley operators, the crystal graph with its edges and the label dictionary.

[F6] Weight modules and integrability ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and the Kashiwara operators ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]) supply the weight grading and the string structure on which [F2]-[F4] operate.

[F1] $T_{0,1}=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}$ is a generator of the integral form
$U_A$; on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ it acts by the Gaussian value
$[\mu(h_1)]_q=\frac{q^{\mu(h_1)}-q^{-\mu(h_1)}}{q-q^{-1}}$, and at $q=1$ this
value is the integer $\mu(h_1)$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]],
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]] (b),
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

(c) **Reordering at $a=b=2$.**
$E^{(2)}F^{(2)}=F^{(2)}E^{(2)}+F^{(1)}T_{i,-2,1}E^{(1)}+T_{i,0,2}$, where
$T_{i,-2,1}=\frac{Kq^{-2}-K^{-1}q^{2}}{q-q^{-1}}$ and
$T_{i,0,2}=\frac{(K-K^{-1})(Kq^{-1}-K^{-1}q)}{(q-q^{-1})(q^{2}-q^{-2})}$; all
three toral binomials are elements of the integral form $U_A$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), and on a weight vector of weight
$\mu$ their $q=1$ values are $\mu(h_i)$, $\mu(h_i)-2$ and
$\binom{\mu(h_i)}{2}$
([[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]]).

[F4] The toral binomials lie in $U_A$, commute with one another and with the
$K_h$, and on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ act by the Gaussian value
$\binom{\mu(h_i)+c}{t}_i$, whose value at $q=1$ is
$\binom{\mu(h_i)+c}{t}$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]],
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]] (b)).

[F2] $[t]!\in A$ and $[t]!\ne0$; the divided powers $E^{(r)},F^{(r)}$, the
$K^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{c,t}$ generate $U_A$; on a weight vector of weight $\mu$
the toral binomial $T_{c,t}$ acts by the Gaussian value
$\binom{\mu(h)+c}{t}_q$, and $E^{(1)},F^{(1)},K^{\pm1},T_{0,1}$ already
preserve $V_A$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]],
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]] (b)).

[F3] On a $U_A$-stable label-graded lattice the specialization has
$\bar K=\mathrm{id}$, $\bar T_{i,c,t}$ acting by the integer binomials and the
classical Cartan commutators; the specialization is defined by base change of
the integral form, never by substituting into rational expressions
([[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]] (b),
[[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]] (c),(d)).

[F3] The $q=1$ comparison ([[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]], [[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]], [[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]], [[lem-local-q-one-deformation-proves-integrable-highest-weight-universality]], [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]): at characteristic-zero $q=1$ the positive toral quotient and the local deformation comparison identify the specialized module with the classical simple integrable highest weight module of the chosen realization, weight by weight, with the classical Weyl–Kac character.

[F4] On a $U_A$-stable label-graded lattice, $\bar K_h=\mathrm{id}$,
$\bar T_{i,c,t}$ acts by $\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c}{t}\in\mathbb Z$, and
the classical Cartan and mixed relations
$[\bar E_i,\bar F_j]=\delta_{ij}\bar H_i$,
$[\bar H_i,\bar E_j]=a_{ij}\bar E_j$,
$[\bar H_i,\bar F_j]=-a_{ij}\bar F_j$ hold
([[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]](b)).

[F2] Local $q=1$ comparison and classical fibre ([[lem-local-q-one-deformation-proves-integrable-highest-weight-universality]], [[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]], [[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]], [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]): the local deformation proves the simple quantum highest weight module and its field character with discrete-valuation-ring-free lattices, and at characteristic-zero $q=1$ the specialization identifies the fibre with the classical simple integrable highest weight module of the regularized realization.

[F3] The $q=1$ comparison ([[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]], [[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]], [[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]], [[lem-local-q-one-deformation-proves-integrable-highest-weight-universality]], [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]): at characteristic-zero $q=1$ the positive toral quotient and the local deformation comparison identify the specialized module with the classical simple integrable highest weight module of the chosen realization, weight by weight, with the classical Weyl–Kac character.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared in [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and used to obtain the decomposition of $M$ into simple integrable highest weight modules from [[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]], which selects a maximal independent family of simple submodules simultaneously. It also permits simultaneous choices of lifts of the finite residue bases in the possibly infinite family of top spaces. After those choices, each lattice and crystal argument is finite and choice-free. No incompatible-axiom branch is used, and no global $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness is assumed. The index set $J$ need not be finite in affine or indefinite type; local weight finiteness means only finitely many summands contribute to any fixed label-weight space.

[F1] Semisimplicity ([[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]], under AC): $M$ is isomorphic to an algebraic direct sum of simple integrable highest weight modules $L(\lambda)$, every nonzero submodule of $M$ contains a maximal vector $v$ with $U_q(\mathfrak g)v\cong L(\lambda)$, and $M$ is the direct sum of the submodules generated by the vectors of any maximal independent family of simple submodules; AC is used exactly to select a maximal independent family of simple submodules simultaneously, and restricted to a module generated by one finite-dimensional $U_q^{\ge0}$-submodule the decomposition is finite and choice-free.

[F3] The integrable highest weight category with finite-dimensional chosen label spaces and support contained in a finite union of downward cones is semisimple: its objects are locally weight-finite direct sums of simple integrable highest weight modules. The decomposition uses the Axiom of Choice as declared by the supplier ([[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]], [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
